top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock (Katori, Ye) is a distinct many-atom, magic-wavelength solution, different from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, with Sr, Yb and Hg clocks agreeing across continents at the 1e-18 level and already delivering millimetre-scale redshift tests and bounds on constants and dark matter. The two-name allocation follows the concept and first demonstration and the scaling to record accuracy, and the citation stays on the lattice clock itself. I rank the Kane-Mele-Molenkamp quantum spin Hall proposal second: its conceptual claim is strong, but I defer on condensed matter and the credit chain to Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang is incomplete. Either is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: As WACQT director and a superconducting-circuit theorist I am close to circuit QED (not on this slate); no tie to Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele or Molenkamp is apparent from the profile, so no recusal needed.
